state: The Can compiler caches generic instances by declaration and concrete arguments and checks whole bodies on a worklist. It currently rejects any ancestry edge to the same declaration when each new argument structurally contains its old argument and some containment is strict. This rejects finite fixed<T> to literal fixed<int[]> when T=int, even though the next target remains int[]. Preloading the array instance makes that same source pass because cache hits bypass the test. True repeat<T> to repeat<T[]> must still be rejected. Inferred calls as well as explicit type applications must behave independently of cache population order. Only argument structures, not nominal fields, are traversed, and a separate finite discovery budget remains. Assess the proposed replacement without claiming a general termination proof.

guard.instructions: Which growth-check refinement best addresses the demonstrated false rejection while keeping a finite implementation and detecting repeated expansion?

criteria.repeated_site: Compare structural growth only when the same declaration recurs through the same source application site along its ancestry; retain the original creation site separately from accumulated request diagnostics. A constant concrete transition then reuses its cache, while repeated growing applications are rejected.
criteria.closed_explicit_only: Keep the declaration-wide growth rule but exempt explicitly written closed type arguments; leave inferred applications under the old containment test.
criteria.keep_rule: Preserve rejection after any structural growth edge to the same declaration and require authors to pre-register fixed target instances in assertions.
